_note: Courting's end (data/marriage.json, README.md, Villagers → Marriage): a candidate's answer to the mizuhiki knot held out (<id>_married, _taken, _waiting, _band, _room; the knot stays in hand), the proposal scene (<id>_yes, data/events/propose_<id>.json) and the wedding at the shrine (<id>_wedding, data/events/wedding_<id>.json). Each part ends with next end. Our own scenes.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Another one? I already have yours, tied to the ledger. One promise is plenty, thank you.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: ...Put that away. That knot is a promise, and yours is already made to somebody else.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Yes, yes, I said yes already. Save it for the shrine. And don't be late.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: A mizuhiki knot? For me? ...Don't. Not yet. We don't know each other that well.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Keep coming by the counter. Then we'll see.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Is that... a mizuhiki knot? Oh. Oh, I see.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: I'd like to say yes. But your farmhouse is one room and a futon. Where would I keep my ledgers?

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Have Hachiro build a second room. Then ask me again. I'll be at the counter.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: That's a mizuhiki knot. Red and white. You know what it means when you hand one over, don't you?

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: I do. Will you marry me?

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: ...Father used to say I'd marry the store. I think I half believed him.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Yes. Yes! I'll keep the store and you'll keep the farm, and we'll keep each other. Deal?

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Grandma Tome will want to ready the shrine. Give her three days. And wear something clean.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Well. The whole village up at the shrine, and not even a festival. Settle down, all of you.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Sayo, your father would have counted every guest and charged them for the tea. He'd be proud.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Now take each other's hands and tie the knot round them both. Tight. A loose knot is a loose promise.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: I'll keep your field in my ledger and you'll keep my shelves in yours. From today, one book.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: One book. I promise.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: Does this mean the store gives us sweets for free now?

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: Hah. It means you'll pay twice, boy. Congratulations, you two.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: There. Done and tied. Off home with you both, and be good to each other.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: You're giving me another? I've only one wrist, and the first one is already on it.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Oh, don't. Your promise is already made to somebody else. Keep that one for them.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: I haven't changed my mind, if that's what you're asking. Three days. I'm counting.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Is that a mizuhiki knot? Put it away before someone sees! ...We've barely shared a pot of tea.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Sit with me a while longer first. A good brew takes its time.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Oh. A knot, red and white. For me?

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: I'd say yes in a heartbeat. But your house is one room, and where would my mother's kettle go?

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Ask Hachiro for a second room. Then come back and ask me properly.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: ...That's a mizuhiki knot. Red and white. You do know what that means?

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: I do. Will you marry me?

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: I told the tea merchant I'd never leave this road. And now somebody asks me to walk down it.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Yes. I'll pour here by day and come home to the hill at night. The kettle comes with me.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Grandma Tome will want three days to ready the shrine. Don't you dare get a cold before then.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Well. The whole village up at the shrine, and not even a festival. Settle down, all of you.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Fumi, your mother poured my tea on that road for forty years. She would weep to see you today.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Now take each other's hands and tie the knot round them both. Tight. A loose knot is a loose promise.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Every morning, the first cup is yours. Every evening, the last. That's my promise.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: And the field's first harvest is yours. I promise.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: ...Hm. Good. Now who pours my tea at lunch?

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: I do, as always. I'm getting married, Ichiro, not moving to the moon.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: There. Done and tied. Off home with you both, and be good to each other.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Another knot? I braided the first one into my sandal strap. One promise is plenty.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Don't. That knot is a promise, and yours is already made to somebody else. Keep it for them.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Yes still means yes. Three days. I'm weaving myself new sandals for the shrine steps.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: A mizuhiki knot? For me? ...Not yet. I don't even know how wide you walk.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Come up the lane more often. Then ask me again.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Red and white, twisted tight... Is that for me?

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: I want to say yes. But your farmhouse is one room, and my straw alone would fill it.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Ask Hachiro for a second room. Then come and find me by the rack.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: That's a mizuhiki knot. Paper cord, twisted tight. I know a good twist when I see one.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: Then you know what it means. Will you marry me?

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: I told everyone I stayed for the hill. That was never all of it.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Yes. I'll weave in Kaminoda by day and walk down to the farm at night. From the lookout I'll wave at our own roof.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Tome will want three days to ready the shrine. I'll need them for a new pair of sandals.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Well. The whole village up at the shrine, and not even a festival. Settle down, all of you.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Haru, your grandmother wove the sandals I was married in. She would be proud to see you on these steps in your own.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Now take each other's hands and tie the knot round them both. Tight. A loose knot is a loose promise.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: A tight weave, then. It lasts. Every afternoon I'll wave from the hill, and every evening I'll come home down it.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: And I'll wave back. Every time. I promise.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Hmph. And who ties my sheaves in the fall?

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: I do, Genzo. I'm marrying the farm down the hill, not leaving the racks.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: There. Done and tied. Off home with you both, and be good to each other.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Another? One's on my wrist already. Doesn't come off in the kiln heat either. Keep it.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: ...No. You promised somebody. A promise is a mark in clay. Leave it be.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Still yes. Three days. I'm beating the soot out of my good jacket.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: ...A knot. For me.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Not yet. Charcoal takes weeks to burn right. So do I.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: ...Red and white. Hm.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Your house is one room. I'm a big man. And I smell of smoke.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Get Hachiro to build a second room. Then ask again.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: ...That's a mizuhiki knot.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Hold it out properly. Both hands. ...Hm. You mean it.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: I do. Will you marry me?

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: My father said a burner marries the kiln. Nobody else will sit in the smoke.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: ...You came up to the smoke anyway. Yes.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Tome needs three days for the shrine. I'll need them to wash. Properly.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Well. The whole village up at the shrine, and not even a festival. Settle down, all of you.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Ichiro, your father brought charcoal to my door every winter and never once stayed for tea. You've grown up kinder.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Now take each other's hands and tie the knot round them both. Tight. A loose knot is a loose promise.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: ...I'm no good with words. So. Every winter, the first piece from the kiln is yours. As long as it burns.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: And I'll sit in the smoke with you. Every burn. I promise.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Years of my rice balls and never a word. Now he gives speeches!

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: ...Hm. Don't get used to it.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: There. Done and tied. Off home with you both, and be good to each other.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Another? Yours is tied round my wrist, wet or dry. One's plenty.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Put it away. Your promise belongs to someone else. I don't fish in other people's water.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Yes is yes. Three days. I'm trying not to go fishing for my nerves.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Whoa, a mizuhiki knot? That's a big catch for such a short line.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Come down to the river more. Then cast again.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Red and white... is that for me?

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: I'd say yes. But your house is one room, and I come with nets, a pole and a smell of fish.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Get Hachiro to add a second room. Then ask me again on the shore.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: That's a mizuhiki knot. You're holding it like a fish you think will jump.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: It won't. Will you marry me?

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Father always said the river takes and never gives back. He never met you.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Yes! Traps at dawn, the farm at night. And the first crossing every morning, for you.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Tome will want three days for the shrine. I'll need them to scrub the river off.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Well. The whole village up at the shrine, and not even a festival. Settle down, all of you.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Mio, your father poled me across to my own wedding. He sang the whole way, badly. I hope you got his heart and not his voice.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Now take each other's hands and tie the knot round them both. Tight. A loose knot is a loose promise.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Tied tight, like a good trap. The first crossing every morning is yours, and every evening I'll come home off the river.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: And every evening I'll be waiting on the bank. I promise.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: Hah. Now who beats me to the best spot on Sundays?

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Me, same as ever. Marriage doesn't make me slower.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: There. Done and tied. Off home with you both, and be good to each other.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Another knot? I tied yours to the shrine rope and to my wrist. One promise, two places. That's plenty.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Please put it away. Your promise is made to someone else. Even the gods keep count.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Still yes! Three days. I've drawn a fortune for each one. All great blessing. Don't ask how.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: A mizuhiki knot? Oh, no, no. Not yet. Even the fox would say it's too soon.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Come up the shrine path more often. Then we'll see what the fortunes say.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Red and white... for me? Oh.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: I want to say yes. But your farmhouse is one room, and I come with an altar, a chest of charms and a great many notebooks.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Ask Hachiro for a second room. Then ask me again at the shrine.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: That's a mizuhiki knot. I've tied a hundred of those for other people's weddings.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: This one is for yours. Will you marry me?

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Grandfather used to say a shrine keeper marries the shrine. I always thought that sounded lonely.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Yes. The shrine by day, you by night. And the first fortune of every year.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Tome will want three days to ready the shrine. My shrine. Oh, this is going to be strange.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Well. The whole village up at the shrine, and not even a festival. Settle down, all of you.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Kaede, I taught you every word of this rite. I never thought I'd say it with you on this side of it.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Now take each other's hands and tie the knot round them both. Tight. A loose knot is a loose promise.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Every New Year the first fortune is yours, and I'll stack the box every time. That's my vow.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: And I'll keep every one you draw. I promise.

lines.speaker: nana
lines.text: Kaede, does this mean no more ghost stories?

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: It means twice as many. Now there's someone at home to scare.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: There. Done and tied. Off home with you both, and be good to each other.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Another knot? I already wove yours into the edge of my best cloth. One is plenty.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Put it away. You've promised someone else. I don't dye over another person's pattern.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Still yes. Three days. I'm dyeing as fast as I can.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: A mizuhiki knot? ...No. Not yet. Cloth that's rushed fades.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Come by the vats more. Let it take the color properly first.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Red and white. For me?

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: I want to say yes. But your farmhouse is one room, and I come with stencils, bolts of cloth and a smell.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Ask Hachiro for a second room. Then ask me again.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: A mizuhiki knot. Red and white. The two colors I've never once dyed.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: Then start with these. Will you marry me?

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: I came home to keep Mother's vats alive. I didn't expect to find anything else here.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Yes. The vats by day, and you the rest of it.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: Tome will want three days to ready the shrine. I'll need every one of them for the sash.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Well. Shino, back from the city and staying for good, it seems. Settle down, everyone.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Your mother stood right here at her own wedding, blue to the wrist like you. She laughed all the way through.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Now take each other's hands and tie the knot round them both. Tight. A loose knot is a loose promise.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: I dipped this sash twenty times for the darkest blue. Every dip was a promise. That's my vow.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: And I'll keep every color you make. I promise.

lines.speaker: kiku
lines.text: Twenty dips, dear! Your mother stopped at twelve.

lines.speaker: shino
lines.text: She said twelve was plenty. I wanted to be sure.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: There. Done and tied. Off home with you both, and be good to each other.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Another knot? I've delivered yours already. To myself. Signed for. One is plenty.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Put it away. That's addressed to someone else. I don't open other people's post.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Still yes! Three days. I've counted the steps from here to the shrine. Two hundred and twelve.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: A mizuhiki knot? For me? Whoa. Hold on. I haven't even finished my letter to you yet.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Walk the round with me a while longer. Then we'll see.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Red and white! For me? Oh.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: I want to say yes. But your farmhouse is one room, and I come with a mailbag, a book pile and very muddy boots.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Ask Hachiro for a second room. Then ask me again. I'll be easy to find. I'm everywhere.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: A mizuhiki knot. I've carried a hundred of these to other people's doors. Nobody ever handed one to me.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: This one is for you. Will you marry me?

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: I know every house in the valley. I never had one to come back to. Just a room behind a counter.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Yes! Yes. The round by day, and home to you. The best address I'll ever have.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Tome will want three days to ready the shrine. I'll deliver the invitations. Fastest post in history.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Well. Ren carried every invitation himself, so of course nobody's late. Settle down, all of you.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Ren, you've brought my son's letters up my path for years. Today I get to give you something back.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Now take each other's hands and tie the knot round them both. Tight. A loose knot is a loose promise.

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Every morning I'll leave from your door, and every evening I'll come back to it. That's my vow.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: And I'll be waiting at the gate. I promise.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Hmph. Who'll bring my seed catalogs on time now?

lines.speaker: ren
lines.text: Me, Genzo. Same as ever. Marriage doesn't slow the post.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: There. Done and tied. Off home with you both, and be good to each other.
